Technical due diligence tool for game publishing deals

CONCEPT MOCKUP

INDIE PUBLISHERS

403 worldwide

Addressable buyers of per-deal diligence, Data40 June 2024

WHAT IT DEMANDS

Technical craft

THE REALITY

FIRST REVENUE

CAPITAL IN

DIFFICULTY

UP AGAINST

Digital Advisors

(digitaladvisors.biz, est.

+ 8 more mapped

THE PITCH

A scout at a mid-size indie publisher gets 500+ submissions a year and signs maybe 10. Over 95% get rejected, often without the build opened end-to-end. The ones that look promising go into a loop one Raw Fury scout calls up to 100 builds long: ask for the next build, repeat. Meanwhile Steam releases hit 18,000 in 2024, and games disclosing generative AI content jumped from about 1,000 in April 2024 to 7,818 by mid-2025. The old shortcut (if the demo looks shippable, the team is probably real) stopped working.

WHO IT'S FOR

Small and midsized game publishers, gaming funds, and studios evaluating playable indie prototypes before signing or acquiring them.

THE GAP

A standardized, signable technical read of the actual prototype, priced below a lawyer and above a dashboard

WHY NOW

AI-made Steam games jumped from 1,000 to 7,818 in about 15 months

AT A GLANCE

WHY NOW

AI-made Steam games jumped from 1,000 to 7,818 in about 15 months

Second, the legal floor moved under publishers' feet. The US Copyright Office's January 2025 report and the D.C. Circuit's March 2025 ruling in Thaler v. Perlmutter confirmed that purely AI-generated works are not copyrightable. Steam's own attestation shifts all copyright liability for AI content onto the developer, and Valve has rejected games on training-data provenance grounds even after full disclosure. A publisher who signs a prototype without checking what is actually under the hood can end up owning a game they cannot defend in court. Third, the money got tighter. Devolver cut average per-game spend from $3M in 2022 to $2M in 2024, with a plan to hit $1M by 2026. A smaller check per deal means fewer deals carry a studio, which means each greenlight has to be right. A $5K technical read against a $1M bet is cheap insurance that did not need to exist two years ago.

The honest counter: Valve narrowed the Steam disclosure rule in January 2026 to cover only player-facing AI output, exempting AI coding assistants and other dev-side tools. That decision tells publishers the platform does not care how the code was written, which could reduce urgency around code-provenance audits specifically. And a market where per-game budgets are falling toward $1M is also a market where some publishers will just add 'no AI assets' to the rejection filter instead of paying for a third-party memo. The timing window is real, but it rewards a product that reads the whole prototype (code, assets, production plan, commercial risk) rather than one that sells 'AI detection' as the headline feature.

MARKET SNAPSHOT

The receipts.

PAIN

7/10 SEVERITY

“Fully AI-generated game assets have no copyright protection under current U.S. law. Your contractor's IP assignment clause may transfer nothing when they use AI tools. Steam requires disclosure before you can ship.”

Promise Legal

“I made the case in a different article that the demo or the build is 80 to 90 percent of a publisher's decision, and that holds true whoever's looking. In gaming, it's seldom the technology, the talent, the patents or something else.”

Game Studio Unlocked Substack · Sebastian Cardoso

“The Cycle: "Not right now but show us the next build!" == infinite cycle of improvements and delays. I can give you feedback and ask for a build, and we could do this 100 times.”

Callum Underwood (Raw Fury scout), slideshare · Callum Underwood

All 8 receipts, and where these people gather

WHITESPACE

MARKET GAP

The gap: a standardized, signable technical read of the actual prototype, priced below a lawyer and above a dashboard

Understand the opening

THE WEDGE

A rapid, standardized greenlight memo that puts code audit, asset provenance, playtesting, production planning, and commercial risk into one comparable format, versus the current mix of internal teams and bespoke solo technical producers.

The incumbent to beat: Digital Advisors

PROOF & SIGNALS

As of June 2024, 403 video game publishers worldwide publish indie games, and 257 do not, per a Data40 survey of 660 publishers.

STATISTA / DATA40

Steam releases jumped from 300 games in 2012 to 8,000 in 2018 to 18,000 in 2024, flooding publisher submission pipelines with 60x more PC titles over 12 years.

GAMEMAKER BLOG / AKUPARA GAMES

The US Copyright Office's January 2025 Copyrightability Report ruled works generated entirely by AI are not copyrightable; the Theatre D'opera Spatial decision denied registration even with 600+ prompts and Photoshop edits, locking in AI-asset provenance as a publisher diligence risk.

PROMISE LEGAL / US COPYRIGHT OFFICE

Veteran game scout Bobby Wertheim says most developers get ghosted not because the game is bad, but because market validation evidence is missing, and in 2025 publishing conditions, 85% of player time goes to older games.

PHOKOU PODCAST WITH BOBBY WERTHEIM
Explore the evidence

WHO YOU'RE UP AGAINST

9 PLAYERS

Digital Advisors

INCUMBENT

(digitaladvisors.biz, est.

Digital Advisors

INCUMBENT

Sells a Game Development Risk Assessment delivered in 4-8 weeks for publishing deal greenlights, acquisitions and investments, with named clients including Aonic, Nomad Games, Megabit Publishing, Creative UK and Baltic Ventures; pricing is not published and all engagements run through a sales call.

GameAcquire

(early access as of October 2026) is a private deal marketplace for buying and selling game studios, IP, prototypes, SDKs and Roblox/UEFN experiences with sample listings priced $45K-$640K; it organizes LOI, diligence and asset-transfer workflow but explicitly does not provide valuation or verification: each party verifies claims and uses outside advisers.

The Powell Group

(powellgroupconsulting.com) sells Game Scouting, Game Viability Assessments, Pitch Deck Consulting and IP Acquisition services to both developers and publishers/investors, with named clients including Humble Games, Mastiff, HyperBeard, Tripwire, Torn Banner, Nightdive and NetEase; pricing is bespoke and the firm also runs the IndieGameBusiness trade event.

GameDiscoverCo

(Simon Carless, 25-year industry veteran) sells Steam/console discoverability data and advises mid-sized publishers including No More Robots, Dotemu and Akupara Games on which games to sign, pricing, and release timing; subscription tiers run $15/mo individual, $500/yr for >20-person companies, with ~20,000 newsletter subscribers.

Game Scout

(gamescout.biz), operated by Gamebiz Consulting in Belgrade, Serbia, profiles 150+ game publishers and offers free plus paid SaaS tools including PitchMaker and Game Filter for both developers and publishers; it is a directory and matching tool, not a diligence product.

Beck Interactive Partners

(Alex Beck, ex-Loaded Games; founded 2024) represents indie developers as a Hollywood-style agent, works with 200+ publishers worldwide, pitched 500+ times in 2025, and operates on zero upfront fees plus rev share; it sits on the opposite side of the deal from publishers but is the organized intermediary that often preps the build.

Fenwick, Reed Smith, Wilson Sonsini

Big law firms (Reed Smith, Fenwick, Wilson Sonsini) run the IP, contractual and regulatory due diligence side of game publisher and studio acquisitions, including Activision Blizzard's acquisition of King; these firms own the legal diligence layer at $500-$1,500/hr but do not open the actual game build.

PEOPLE ARE ASKING FOR IT

REDDIT

“The game was fast approaching release and the problem was that the marketing had been extremely thin and largely ineffective, and their external QA had found maybe fifty percent of what a competent internal pass would have caught. All of this was going to be…”

Game Studio Unlocked (Sebastian Cardoso) · Sebastian Cardoso

“If the publisher's acceptance standard is subjective, "commercially acceptable quality" or "satisfactory to publisher", the publisher effectively holds a veto over your funding. A publisher can withhold acceptance (and therefore payment) for reasons that have…”

Promise Legal · Promise Legal Staff

“95%+ of game submissions from external developers get rejected. Product development (PD) professionals are swamped – these are very busy people. There are entirely too many game submissions from too many developers to keep track of for most publishers.…”

Game Developer (Gil Winters) · Gil Winters

THE VERDICT

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

The timing hook is not vibes: Steam AI disclosures went from about 1,000 games in April 2024 to 7,818 by mid-2025, and the US Copyright Office ruled in January 2025 that purely AI works are not copyrightable, so whoever signs the deal eats the provenance risk.
A named incumbent (Digital Advisors) already sells the bespoke version in 4-8 weeks to Aonic, Nomad Games and Megabit Publishing, which proves publishers will pay a third party for this work; you win by productizing it to 7 days at $4,500 flat.
Pricing has real headroom: gaming consultants bill $10K-$40K per project and $4K-$25K/month on retainer, mid-size publishers already pay $50K-$75K for junior scouts, so a $4,500 memo and $7,500/mo retainer read as cheap, not expensive.
The buyer list is small enough to work by hand: 403 named indie publishers worldwide, 150+ already profiled by Game Scout, meaning an insider can personally cover the entire addressable market in a quarter.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Zero inbound search demand on every solution term (game technical due diligence, game code audit, game asset provenance all show 0 searches/mo on Google Ads), so every one of the first 100 customers comes from direct outreach or warm intro, and a non-insider will get ghosted.
The ceiling is capped: with 403 total publishers and maybe 60 that sign enough deals to retainer, the honest annual ceiling is $3.5M-$4.5M ARR, which is a lifestyle business not a VC outcome, and a single churned anchor is a material revenue event.
IP and NDA risk is existential: publishers may refuse to share builds with a third party, and one leaked prototype ends the business, so the trust bar to even see the build is higher than any dashboard tool has had to clear.
Incumbents can copy the format in a quarter: Digital Advisors already does the work, GameDiscoverCo already owns the publisher relationships, so the only durable moat is a benchmark dataset of 200+ reviewed prototypes that only exists after you have shipped it.
Roast it with your agent

FOUNDER FIT

Not every good idea is good for you.

WHO IT’S BEST FOR

Technical founders with game development background
Teams with AI analytics expertise
Entrepreneurs experienced in B2B SaaS
Non-technical founders without AI knowledge
Founders unfamiliar with game publishing

An ex-publisher scout or senior technical producer who has shipped 2+ titles, personally knows 20+ scouts at mid-size publishers, and can read Unity or Unreal code in a day. They do not need to be a strong engineer by AAA standards; they need to be the person a Humble or No More Robots scout already texts for a gut check. The second-best builder is an indie dev who shipped a game that got signed, got burned by vague milestone language, and now sells the fix back to publishers. The worst fit is a pure SaaS founder with no games network trying to productize a service they have never delivered.

THE PLAN

If you started today.
First up.

Search is dead for this category. Every solution-specific term (game technical due diligence, game code audit, game asset provenance) returns zero monthly searches on Google Ads. Publishers do not type this problem into Google. They solve it by calling a scout they know or hiring a technical producer for the week. The whole acquisition motion is relationship-led and outbound. summary.section_the_plan:
If you started today.
First up.

Search is dead for this category. Every solution-specific term (game technical due diligence, game code audit, game asset provenance) returns zero monthly searches on Google Ads. Publishers do not type this problem into Google. They solve it by calling a scout they know or hiring a technical producer for the week. The whole acquisition motion is relationship-led and outbound. Any plan that depends on content marketing or SEO to drive inbound leads will starve.

See the detailed plan
Year one, on a napkin.
